meta.title: Therapeutic ICD Survey
meta.description: Quantify how the mix of current ICD device types may shift as four new therapeutic device concepts enter the market sequentially; estimate incremental penetration among patients who are currently ICD-indicated but untreated; assess the potential to expand device therapy to newly eligible patients, particularly those with an ejection fraction of 40%–50%; and identify the primary adoption drivers and barriers for each concept. Blinded study among ICD implanters and referring physicians in the United States, Italy and Germany; n=270; approximately 25 minutes.

questions.text:
Thank you for taking the time to respond to our survey. We are conducting research among healthcare professionals involved in the management of heart-failure patients and the use of cardiac implantable electronic devices. We are not selling anything.

If you qualify, the survey should take approximately 25 minutes. Because you will be shown product information, we recommend completing the survey on a desktop or laptop computer, or another device with a large screen.

Your responses will remain anonymous and confidential, and will only be reviewed in aggregate with those of other healthcare professionals.

Please use the navigation buttons at the bottom of the screen. Do not use your browser's Back button.

questions.text:
Next we would like you to evaluate some new device concepts from a major medical device manufacturer such as Abbott, Boston Scientific or Medtronic.

For the purposes of this survey, we have randomly assigned you to one of the major manufacturers. You have been assigned to MEDTRONIC.

This information is highly confidential, and it is important that we obtain your honest and open feedback so that the best possible product can be developed for the market.

When reviewing, please assume the following:

  • It is approved for use by the regulatory agencies in your country.
  • It performs in accordance with the information shown in the description.
  • It is available on the market for your hospital or facility to consider.

questions.text: Finally, we have a few questions for classification purposes.
